theory.title: Either…or and neither…nor
theory.explanation: Use either…or to present two alternatives and neither…nor to say that both alternatives are excluded. The verb usually agrees with the subject closest to it: Neither the manager nor the assistants are available.
theory.tip: Either…or ofrece dos alternativas; neither…nor excluye ambas.

content.passage: A customer was offered two ways to solve a problem. The shop could either replace the faulty item or give a full refund. The customer could contact the service team either by phone or by email. Neither the manager nor the assistants were available that afternoon, so the customer sent a message. Neither the price nor the quality had been the main issue; the problem was the late delivery.

content.audioTranscript: A: I'm calling about my order. B: Do you have the receipt? A: Yes. The customer service told me I could get a refund. B: Was there a problem with the delivery? A: Yes, so I asked to speak to the manager. B: I'll contact the supplier and check the payment. A: Thank you. Is the parcel going to the right address? B: Yes, it should arrive tomorrow.
